blockingFindings.title: Conflict-id disambiguation rule is undefined for cross-scope code literals
blockingFindings.body:
**Target:** R2 / src/flow/lib/task-scope.js (BROAD_STEPS), src/flow/lib/gate-step.js, src/flow/registry.js
**Issue:** The spec defines how to disambiguate the three conflict ids (review/gate-impl/impl) only for definition.js structure (FLOW vs TASK position) and for the migration tool's flow.json (steps[] vs tasks[].steps[]). But these ids also appear as bare string literals in shared/cross-scope runtime code that the spec never analyzed. The clearest hazard is src/flow/lib/task-scope.js: `BROAD_STEPS = ["implement", "review", "gate-impl"]` mixes a flow-leaf id (`implement`, on the unchanged list) with two conflict ids (`review`, `gate-impl`). Because `implement`≠`impl`, it is indeterminate from the spec whether broad-mode steps map to flow names (impl-review / impl-gate) or task names (task-review / task-gate). gate-step.js also hardcodes `"gate-impl"` (TASK_STEP_TO_PHASE) and a `"gate"` fallback, and registry.js's REVIEW_RUNTIME_STEP_BY_PHASE hardcodes `impl: "review"`. The spec's [VERIFY] decisions did not cover these sites; R2's blanket 'update all references to new names' gives no rule for choosing the correct scope-specific new name at these mixed-scope call sites.
**Required change:** Add to R2 (or the rename mapping) the explicit new-name target for each conflict-id literal at the cross-scope code sites — at minimum task-scope.js BROAD_STEPS, gate-step.js TASK_STEP_TO_PHASE/`gate` fallback, and registry.js REVIEW_RUNTIME_STEP_BY_PHASE — stating which scope (flow→impl-*/spec-gate, task→task-*) each resolves to.
**Why blocking:** If BROAD_STEPS' `review`/`gate-impl` are renamed to the wrong scope, createBroadModeRecord/assertAuditedBroadMode validation and `sdd-forge flow set broad --step <id>` will reject the legitimate step id (or accept a wrong one), breaking broad-mode execution; similarly a wrong choice in the review/gate post-hook resolution silently mis-resolves the in-progress step. The unit-test updates in R4 could be edited to the same wrong name, so the defect would not be caught — implementation cannot proceed correctly without the scope rule for these sites.

nonBlockingImprovements.title: grep-0 acceptance is ambiguous for bare ids review/gate/impl
nonBlockingImprovements.target: R5 / Acceptance Criteria (authored sources + installed copies grep 0 件)
nonBlockingImprovements.body:
**Target:** R5 / Acceptance Criteria (authored sources + installed copies grep 0 件)
**Improvement:** Specify the match precision for the grep-0 check on the bare old ids review/gate/impl. As written, a literal grep cannot reach 0 because the new names (impl-review, spec-gate, task-impl, etc.) and ordinary English text contain these tokens as substrings/components. Recommend anchoring to step-id literal form (e.g. quoted ids) or word boundaries excluding hyphen-joined compounds.
**Why non-blocking:** A competent implementer can choose a sensible anchored grep pattern; the rename itself is implementable and verifiable, only the exactness of the verification command needs tightening.

nonBlockingImprovements.title: flow.json nested step traversal not stated for the migration tool
nonBlockingImprovements.body:
**Target:** R7 / Decisions (flow.json 構造判別)
**Improvement:** Flow steps in flow.json are a tree (gate-step.js flattenForGate recurses s.children); the conflict id impl-review sits under the nested impl branch. State that the tool must traverse nested children within top-level steps[] (flow scope) rather than only the top level.
**Why non-blocking:** ‘構造位置で判別’ reasonably implies recursing the flow tree, and the flow-vs-task scope distinction (steps[] vs tasks[].steps[]) is unaffected by depth, so the migration intent is still derivable.

nonBlockingImprovements.target: T-7 / R7 (--apply は実行前に git clean を検証)
nonBlockingImprovements.body:
**Target:** T-7 / R7 (--apply は実行前に git clean を検証)
**Improvement:** Note that running the migration with --apply inside worktree 269 requires all prior task changes (T-1..T-6) to be committed first so the working tree is clean, then the apply produces its single commit (T-8 ordering). A one-line sequencing note would prevent a confusing precondition failure.
**Why non-blocking:** The constraint is resolvable by ordinary commit sequencing the implementer controls; it does not make the task impossible or change what must be built.
